description: The pure (modulo semantic strings) port of BFO to Lean 4. Also available at https://github.com/BuildCoherence/bfo-to-lean.

Basic Formal Ontology: wraps bfo-raw, declaring every BFO universal as a rigid universal and every BFO relation as a raw single-sorted relation form (slots at the weakest covering universal; exact domain/range constraints stay enforced by the adopted BFO axioms). A single open of the file id adopts names and classification instances together.

Macro library defining the universal, rigid universal, and relation commands that expand into plain definitions over shared time-indexed classification classes — content-identified, so identical declarations in different files are definitionally equal. Activate the commands with `open scoped <file id>`; declarations work at the top level of a file, no wrapping namespace required.
Provides the LogicIsActual bridge axioms (intro, K-axiom modus ponens, consistency, idempotence) that let you carry Lean's logical entailment into reasoning about actuality.
Adds the prefix notation A p as shorthand for Axiom.Actual p.

Defines the bare ModalWorld structure — a possible world as a normal modal operator with the same properties as ActualBridge provides Actual. Meant to be extended by another structure to create a specific hypothetical world.

Formalizes the ethical claim that murdering a child deserves greater punishment than an otherwise-identical non-child murder, and proves it holds Actually for a concrete two-victim example given the principle and case facts.

Formalizes an argument that 21st-century animal agriculture is impermissible — chaining that it enslaves mammals (who can experience via their CNS), that enslaving experiencers causes harm, and that unnecessary harm is impermissible — and proves ¬ A (Permissible AnimalAg21Cent).

Formalizes a counterfactual ("if the Nazis had won WWII, German would be the USA's official language") by modeling a NazisWonWWIIWorld that forks from the actual world at 1939, demonstrating the semantic-string-to-formal-definition bridge.
